findings.title: Invalid Ruby `end if` breaks the embed view template
findings.body: Line 6 contains `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The bare `if` with no condition is a syntax error: counting the if/each blocks in this file, there are 4 opening block keywords (the `if` at line 2, the orphan `if` created by `end if`, the `if` at line 11, and the `each do` at line 12) but only 3 `end` tokens total in the whole file (lines 6, 22, 29). This means the template will fail to compile with a Ruby SyntaxError (missing `end`), so every request to `EmbedController#best` that reaches a found topic will raise an error instead of rendering, breaking the entire embed feature that this PR introduces.

findings.title: cook_method raw_html bypasses all HTML sanitization for RSS-imported content
findings.body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` unmodified when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping `PrettyText`/`post_analyzer.cook` entirely. `TopicEmbed.import` (used directly by `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`) always uses this cook method, but unlike `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (which runs content through Readability's whitelist of tags/attributes), the RSS/feed path passes feed item content straight through (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) with no tag or attribute whitelist at all. Since `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders this with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, any script/markup present in a polled RSS/Atom feed item is stored and rendered verbatim, enabling stored XSS for anyone who can influence the configured feed's content.

findings.title: Unescaped URL interpolated into href attribute enables markup/attribute injection
findings.body: `contents << "...#{url}..."` inserts `url` directly into an HTML attribute without escaping. `url` is only validated with `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (anchors the start only; arbitrary characters, including single quotes, are allowed afterward) and can originate from end-user input (the `embed_url` controller param is passed through `TopicRetriever`/`TopicEmbed.import_remote` into this method) or from a polled feed item link. A URL containing a single quote (e.g. `http://host/'onmouseover='alert(1)`) breaks out of the `href='...'` attribute and injects an arbitrary attribute/markup. Because the resulting post uses `cook_method: raw_html` (which bypasses sanitization, see Post#cook) and is rendered with `raw`, this is exploitable stored HTML/JS injection.

findings.title: Check-then-create race on embed_url can raise an unhandled unique-constraint error
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` reads `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`, and if blank, later calls `TopicEmbed.create!` inside the same `Topic.transaction`. There is a unique index on `embed_url` (see the `create_topic_embeds` migration), so two concurrent calls for the same not-yet-imported URL will race: both see `embed.blank?` as true, both create a Topic/Post, and the second `create!` raises an unhandled DB uniqueness error which rolls back that transaction. This can realistically happen because `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttling is bypassed entirely for staff users (`no_throttle: true` from `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`), and concurrent `PollFeed` runs/imports of the same item are also possible, leaving an unhandled exception surfacing from the job.

findings.title: Full RSS feed poll triggered synchronously for every unresolved embed request
findings.body: When `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, `perform_retrieve` synchronously executes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` — fetching and parsing the entire configured feed and importing every item — any time a user requests an embed for a URL that is not yet in `topic_embeds`, even if that URL has nothing to do with the feed. The per-URL throttle in `retrieved_recently?` only limits repeated requests for the *same* embed_url; many distinct unknown URLs (or bursts of requests) will each trigger a full, redundant feed fetch with no rate limiting on the feed-poll operation itself, creating unnecessary load on both this server and the remote feed source.

findings.title: feed_key is defined but never used
findings.body: `feed_key` builds a Redis-style key based on a SHA1 of the feed URL, presumably intended for tracking feed modification state (e.g. to skip reprocessing an unchanged feed via conditional GET), but it is never referenced anywhere in `Jobs::PollFeed` or elsewhere. As written, every hourly run re-downloads and re-parses the entire feed and re-imports every item from scratch, which is wasted work; this looks like an incomplete feature left behind in the PR.

findings.title: New gems added outside dual-boot conditional, but only one lockfile updated
findings.body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally in the Gemfile (lines 210-211), outside the `if rails4? ... else ... end` block, meaning they apply to both the Rails 3 and Rails 4 boot modes that this Gemfile's custom Bundler monkeypatch supports (via separate lockfiles, e.g. `Gemfile_rails4.lock` vs the default lockfile). Only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated in this PR; the default (Rails 3) lockfile is not shown as updated. If Rails-3 mode is still used (e.g. CI or deployment with `RAILS3` set), `bundle install`/`bundle check` would fail because the Gemfile and its lockfile are out of sync.

findings.title: Disqus import task silently drops category assignment and original timestamp
findings.body: Previously, importing a Disqus thread created the topic with `category: category_id` (derived from the `-c/--category` option) and `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, preserving the original thread date and allowing categorization. This PR removes the `method_option :category` entirely and replaces the manual `PostCreator` call with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which has no way to specify a category or a custom `created_at`. Anyone invoking this thor task with `-c`/`--category` will now get a Thor "unknown option" error, and all imported Disqus threads will be timestamped at import time rather than their original creation date — an undocumented behavioral regression.

findings.title: Prerequisite-setting tests don't isolate the condition under test
findings.body: In "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username", only the setting under test is stubbed; `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is left at its real default (`false`, per `config/site_settings.yml`). Since `execute` short-circuits on `feed_polling_enabled?` first, both tests pass trivially regardless of whether the url/username checks work correctly — they would still pass even if those specific checks were removed from `execute`. The tests give false confidence and don't actually verify the url/username guard clauses.

findings.title: Weak postMessage origin check using substring containment instead of equality
findings.body: `postMessageReceived` validates the sender using `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. it checks whether `e.origin` appears anywhere as a substring of `discourseUrl`, rather than comparing the two for equality (or checking that `discourseUrl` starts with `e.origin`). This is a looser check than a proper origin comparison and can behave unexpectedly depending on how `discourseUrl` is configured (e.g. trailing path segments, protocol differences), weakening the intended protection against processing resize messages from untrusted origins.

findings.title: absolutize_urls mishandles protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: `absolutize_urls` treats any `href`/`src` starting with `/` as site-relative and rewrites it to `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. For a protocol-relative URL like `//cdn.example.com/image.png`, `start_with?('/')` is true, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `cdn.example.com/image.png`, which then gets rewritten to `http://<originalhost>/cdn.example.com/image.png` — a broken URL pointing at the wrong host/path instead of the intended external resource. Any imported content (RSS or scraped article) using protocol-relative links/images will render broken links/images.

findings.title: Controller spec never enables render_views, so the broken embed template is never exercised
findings.body: This spec (and the rest of the test suite for this feature) never sets `render_views true`. RSpec controller specs default to stubbing out the view-rendering layer, so `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` — which contains an invalid `end if` that breaks compilation (see separate finding) — is never actually rendered by any test in this PR. This allowed a template that cannot compile to be merged without any test catching it.

findings.title: force: true added to an already-existing migration; also added with an earlier timestamp than this PR's new migrations
findings.body: This migration already existed prior to the PR and is modified here to add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`, which will silently drop the existing `top_topics` table (and any data in it) if the migration is ever re-applied against an environment where that table already exists. Additionally, the two new migrations added in this PR (`20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` and `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb`) carry earlier timestamps than this already-existing migration (`20131223171005`), which is unusual ordering for newly added migrations and can cause confusion about intended apply order across environments.
